Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick acknowledgement and initial answers below; I’ve looped in Rohan (policy/compliance) and Monica (customer success) to produce the formal attestation and DPIA summary.

High-level answers (so you can keep moving):
- Intent & collection: Redwood Inference does not design the platform to target children and does not have business processes that intentionally collect children’s personal data. We are an inference platform — customers are responsible for the data they send to the API. That said, the platform can process any payload customers submit, so we rely on customer-side controls and contractual commitments where appropriate.

- Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: By default, the Hosted API does not perform age-based filtering for incoming requests. Customers using Dedicated or Private deployments can configure network/policy controls in front of the runtime (and we support deployment-time integrations with WAFs and reverse proxies). We can provide guidance and a reference age-gating flow.

- Age-gating controls: We offer guidance and reference patterns (see attached "age_gate_flow.png") for customer-implemented gating at ingestion and recommend combining client-side checks + server-side verification. We also have a set of recommended prompt-filtering rules and a simple webhook-based pre-processing hook customers can use to block requests failing age checks.

- DPIA/mitigations: Typical mitigations include token-level retention limits, KV cache eviction policies, configurable log retention, and optional end-to-end encryption in Private deployments. Rohan will produce a short DPIA summary that maps these mitigations to common DPIA questions.

Next steps: Rohan / Monica — can you prepare a one-page attestation (signed PDF) that we can share with EduForge, and a 1–2 page DPIA summary? Samir — is it OK if we also include our SOC 2 scope statement and a brief note about contractual clauses (SCCs / DPA) in the packet?

Hi Samir — apologies for the delay; attaching the requested materials. Below is a concise attestation and summary.

Attestation (summary):
Redwood Inference hereby attests that, as of the date below, Redwood does not knowingly target or solicit personal information from children under the age of 13 via its Hosted API. Redwood’s platform processes data submitted by customers; customers are responsible for user-facing collection mechanisms (including parental consent and client-side age gating). For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers retain greater control over ingress controls and may deploy vendor-provided or customer-provided gating solutions. Redwood will cooperate with customers to support contractual commitments related to COPPA compliance, including DPA addenda and SCCs where applicable.

DPIA summary (high-level):
- Data minimization: recommend limiting prompt inputs to only fields required for inference.
- Retention: runtime token logs are retained by default for 30 days and can be shortened per contract; KV cache has configurable eviction and TTL policies; Dedicated/Private can opt for zero-retention configurations for logs.
- Access controls: role-based access to logs and model telemetry; audit logging enabled for admin actions.
- Technical controls: optional encryption-at-rest for customer-managed volumes in Private deployments; in-flight TLS; config options to disable persistent caching for sensitive projects.
- Contractual controls: Redwood offers a standard DPA with SCCs and will include an education addendum for customers in the K-12 space.

Attachments sent: redwood-attestation-signed.pdf (signed attestation), DPIA_summary_EduForge_redwood.pdf (2 pages), age_gate_flow.png (reference diagram), redwood-coppa-faq.pdf (FAQ & recommended controls).
